title: Open immersions and open restriction for $f^!$
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes and morphisms below are in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: schemes are separated and of finite type over $k$, and morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ be admissible, with the condensed coefficient convention and localizing closures of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $\mathcal T_T=\Loc(\Dctf(T,\Lambda))\subset D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$, where $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\Dctf$ means bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Write $f^!$ for the compactification-independent Brown right adjoint on these categories [det-sf-existence-brown], and $j_!=D(j_!)$ for levelwise extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek; sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek].

1. For a quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\to X$ with $X$ qcqs [def-weil-open-immersion; def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], the functor $j_!:\mathcal T_U\to\mathcal T_X$ is left adjoint to $j^*:\mathcal T_X\to\mathcal T_U$, and $j^!\simeq j^*$ canonically, compatibly with the adjunctions.
2. For $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type, an open immersion $v:V\to Y$, $X_V=f^{-1}(V)$, $u:X_V\to X$ and $f_V:X_V\to V$, there is a canonical isomorphism $u^*f^!\simeq f_V^!v^*$ of functors $\mathcal T_Y\to\mathcal T_{X_V}$; for an open $j:U\to X$ there is a canonical isomorphism $j^*f^!\simeq(fj)^!$ of functors $\mathcal T_Y\to\mathcal T_U$.
3. A morphism in $\mathcal T_X$ is an isomorphism as soon as its restrictions to the members of an open covering $X=\bigcup_aU_a$ are. The preceding canonical comparisons compute the restrictions of $f^!$ on $X$ and $Y$: $j_a^*f^!\simeq(fj_a)^!$, and for $Y=\bigcup_bV_b$, $u_b^*f^!\simeq f_{V_b}^!v_b^*$.

proof.text: On module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] supplies the exact adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$. The coefficient identification of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] makes $j^*$ exact, with the action transported along $\alpha_j^{-1}$. For either functor $H$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives the termwise functor $D(H)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identifies it as both total derived functors. Here are explicit data for the ind/pro convention in [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]. At a right index $s:K\to K'$, put $p_s=D(H)(s)^{-1}$, choose the identity index and identity splitting. For $ts=s'$, $p_{s'}D(H)(t)=p_s$. Taking the common target to be $s$ itself makes the factorization in [def-pc-essentially-constant-ind-diagram] equal $D(H)(s)D(H)(s)^{-1}=1$. Dually, at a left index $s:K'\to K$, take $u_s=D(H)(s)^{-1}$, the identity index and identity retraction. At the common source $s$ the criterion in [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram] is $D(H)(s)^{-1}D(H)(s)=1$. These systems are therefore essentially constant with value $D(H)K$.

source.place: Proof (1); Stacks derived.tex Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, and categories.tex Tag 05PU, definition-essentially-constant-diagram.

proof.text: The homotopy functors used in these systems exist: [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] gives preservation of homotopies and the termwise adjunction on homotopy categories for the additive adjoint pair in step 1. The existence conditions of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] have just been verified at every complex. Apply it with $G=j_!$ and $F=j^*$ to obtain the canonical adjunction $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$ on the ambient unbounded module-object derived categories.

By [det-proper-image-localizing-open], $D(j_!)$ preserves $\Dctf$, sums and the localizing hulls; [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] gives the same hull preservation for $j^*$. Both restricted functors therefore exist. The subcategories $\mathcal T_U,\mathcal T_X$ are full by [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For $M\in\mathcal T_U$, $N\in\mathcal T_X$, their Hom sets are the ambient Hom sets, so the step 2 bijection $\Hom(j_!M,N)\cong\Hom(M,j^*N)$ restricts, with the same naturality and triangle identities. This proves the adjunction on precisely the localizing categories in clause (1).

source.place: Proof (1), preservation of the localizing subcategories and restriction of the adjunction.

proof.text: The compact-generation hypotheses for the Brown adjunction are supplied by [sk-lem-brown-hypotheses] for every standing source scheme. Compute the lower shriek for $j$ using $U\xrightarrow jX\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_X}X$, which is a compactification in the sense of [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]: $j$ is quasi-compact open and the identity is proper. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] its functor is $R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\circ D(j_!)$. Here $R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*$ is the total right derived functor of $\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_{\mathrm{id}}}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(\mathrm{id}^{\Ab}_*)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]; since $\eta_{\mathrm{id}}$ is the identity of $\Lambda_X$, this underived functor is the identity of $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, which is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] (1) the termwise functor $D(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ is a right derived functor of it, so by uniqueness of Kan extensions $R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ canonically and $R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*D(j_!)\cong D(j_!)$; no resolution hypothesis is needed. Step 3 exhibits $j^*$ as a right adjoint of $D(j_!)$, hence, through this isomorphism, of the lower shriek for this compactification. Clause (3) of [det-sf-existence-brown] now gives the unique adjunction-compatible isomorphism $j^!\simeq j^*$, including transport from the chosen compactification. Thus the comparison is canonical with respect to both unit and counit, not an arbitrary isomorphism of functors.

source.place: Proof (1), trivial compactification and uniqueness; compactification is as in sk-def-nagata-sketch-data.

proof.text:
The compact-generation hypotheses for the Brown adjunction are supplied by [sk-lem-brown-hypotheses] for every standing source scheme. We spell out the composition input instead of applying the conditional finite-Tor lemma lem-sf-mate. For composable standing morphisms $T\xrightarrow aS\xrightarrow bR$, the natural lower-shriek comparison $Rb_!Ra_!\cong R(ba)_!$ on $\mathcal T_T$ is [lem-sfb-nonrational-localizing-lower-shriek-composition] when $\Lambda=A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E$, and [lem-sfb-localizing-lower-shriek-composition] when $\Lambda=E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is its case $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. By [det-sf-existence-brown], all three right adjunctions exist on these same categories. For $M\in\mathcal T_T$ and $N\in\mathcal T_R$, compose their Hom bijections and the lower-shriek comparison to get
$$\Hom(M,a^!b^!N)\cong\Hom(Ra_!M,b^!N)\cong\Hom(Rb_!Ra_!M,N)\cong\Hom(R(ba)_!M,N)\cong\Hom(M,(ba)^!N).$$
This is natural in $M,N$. By [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] it gives a unique isomorphism $a^!b^!\cong(ba)^!$: the inverse natural Hom transformation gives the inverse map, since their composites are identity transformations of representables. Naturality in $N$ follows from faithfulness of the same Yoneda functor. The two successive adjunction bijections are the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], so this is the comparison compatible with the pasted units and counits. No ambient exceptional adjunction or six-functor-datum hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: Proof (1), Hom calculation used by the detail item proof (2).

proof.text: All standing schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since fields are Noetherian. By [def-weil-constructible-subset] their opens and intersections with affine opens are quasi-compact. Every such open inclusion is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], and a monomorphism, so its diagonal is an isomorphism and it is separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Composing open inclusions with the finite-type structure maps and with $f$ preserves finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The diagonal of a source restriction of $f$ is the restriction of its closed diagonal, so it remains closed. Finally [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] gives the separated finite-type property of $f_V$. Thus $U,V,X_V$, their structure maps, $u,v,j,fj,f_V$ all have the standing hypotheses required by steps 4 and 5.

source.place: Proof (2), geometric hypotheses for both restrictions.

proof.text:
In the Cartesian open square, $u$ includes $f^{-1}(V)$ and the actual scheme morphisms satisfy $fu=vf_V$. Steps 4 and 5, with their adjunction-compatible natural isomorphisms, give
$$u^*f^!\cong u^!f^!\cong(fu)^!=(vf_V)^!\cong f_V^!v^!\cong f_V^!v^*.$$
The middle equality is transport along $fu=vf_V$ for the same lower-shriek functor and its canonical adjoint. Applying the same steps to $(j,f)$ gives $j^*f^!\cong j^!f^!\cong(fj)^!$. This proves both comparisons in clause (2), natural on the full localizing categories.

Replace the index family by its set of distinct opens in the fixed universe, hence a small family. For $\phi:K\to L$ in $\mathcal T_X$, choose a distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow\phi L\to C\to K[1]$. Exactness of restriction [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] and [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] show that $j_a^*C=0$ when all $j_a^*\phi$ are isomorphisms. Exact module pullback [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] give $j_a^*\mathcal H^n(C)\cong\mathcal H^n(j_a^*C)=0$ for every integer $n$.

The underlying abelian-sheaf functor of module pullback is inverse image, with transported coefficient action, by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. For an open immersion it is the pullback of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star], computed by [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction] as $(j_a^*G)(T\to U_a)\cong G(T\to U_a\to X)$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (1), the site $(U_a)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ is the slice $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}/U_a$. Consequently the underlying abelian sheaf $G_n$ of $\mathcal H^n(C)$ restricts to zero on each such slice. A module with zero underlying sheaf is zero: the unique arrows to and from zero commute with its action, and their composites are identities. This needs no interchange of a forgetful functor with cohomology.

Check the covering-sieve hypothesis of [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism]. For every site object $T\to X$, the opens $T_a=T\times_XU_a$ cover $T$. These are site objects by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (1) and (4), applied also to $T_a\subset T$. For each affine open $W\subset T$, principal affine opens form a basis, so quasi-compactness of $W$ supplies finitely many principal opens $D(s_i)\subset W$, each contained in some $T_{a_i}$, which cover $W$. They are affine opens in $T_{a_i}$ as well. Each $T_a\to T$ is flat because its maps on local rings are isomorphisms. Thus the family is fpqc by the affine-cover criterion in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], including $W=\varnothing$ with the empty refinement. The sieve on $T$ of arrows whose domain maps to some $U_a$ contains this family, and hence covers by [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site]. This argument asserts finiteness only over each affine $W$, not over an arbitrary site object $T$.

source.place: Proof (3), covering-sieve hypothesis of sheaf-local detection.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] to $0\to G_n$. Step 9 identifies its slice restrictions as isomorphisms, and step 10 verifies its covering-sieve hypothesis; hence $G_n=0$. The module observation of step 9 makes $\mathcal H^n(C)=0$ for all $n$. A representative complex $C^\bullet$ is acyclic, so $0\to C^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism and is inverted by the localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Therefore $C=0$; [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] implies that $\phi$ is invertible. Since $\mathcal T_X$ is full by [sk-def-localizing-closure], its ambient inverse lies in this subcategory. No bound on the cohomological degrees of $C$ was used.

source.place: Proof (3), vanishing and detection of isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply clause (2), proved in step 7, to each $j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow X$ and to each $v_b:V_b\hookrightarrow Y$. This gives $j_a^*f^!\cong(fj_a)^!$ and $u_b^*f^!\cong f_{V_b}^!v_b^*$ for the whole localizing categories. Step 11 detects isomorphisms after these restrictions. These are exactly the locality and isomorphism-detection assertions of clause (3). For an empty scheme the same argument says all cohomology sheaves are zero; for the identity cover the comparisons reduce to the same adjunction bijections.

source.place: Proof (3), final two sentences, read as the explicit comparisons in the statement.
